title: Are there undiscovered people?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss whether undiscovered peoples still exist, prompted by 2008 news photos of an uncontacted tribe in Brazil. They distinguish "undiscovered" from "uncontacted" or "isolated" peoples, cover the history of colonial enslavement and genocide, the Akuntsu (spelled "accun Zoo" in the transcript) massacre in Brazil, the Sentinelese of North Sentinel Island, disease as a threat to isolated groups, savage tourism, and protective laws in Brazil, Peru and Paraguay. The episode closes with listener mail about organ donation and anonymity between donors and recipients, from an anesthesiologist, and a thank-you to Dan of Dan Made pottery.

segments.title: Opening banter and 2008 undiscovered tribe news
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter, then introduce news photos from 2008 of people in longhouses in Brazil aiming bows at a low-flying helicopter, which newspapers called undiscovered.

segments.title: Undiscovered versus uncontacted
segments.summary: Chuck criticizes press coverage, noting the Independent's framing and that the group was not undiscovered; an expert who had followed them for twenty years says they were known. The hosts settle on the terms uncontacted or isolated.

segments.title: Can anyone still be undiscovered?
segments.summary: Hosts discuss how satellite and GPS mapping have covered nearly all land, though some primitive groups remain isolated. They note unknown self-names and the group Survival International.

segments.title: History of enslavement and colonial conquest
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the historical enslavement of newly met peoples, including Columbus and the Arawak, African slavery systems, and how old maps labeled unexplored lands with monsters, encouraging fear of outsiders.

segments.title: Akuntsu massacre and violence against isolated tribes
segments.summary: Hosts describe how logging, soy, and cattle interests in Brazil led to the massacre of the Akuntsu by armed men, leaving seven survivors, and the more recent report of only five living.

segments.title: Sentinelese of North Sentinel Island
segments.summary: Hosts describe the Sentinelese on North Sentinel Island in the Andaman Islands, considered among the most isolated peoples, who came to the beach for coconuts thrown by visitors and who use recovered metal from shipwrecks.

segments.title: Disease, contact risks, and protective laws
segments.summary: Hosts explain that disease is a bigger threat than violence, citing historical epidemics and the 1980s Zoe contact that killed 45 members, and more recent contact that hit the Mashco-Piro (spoken as Maroon whoa). They also discuss savage tourism and protections in Brazil, Peru, and Paraguay.

segments.title: Listener mail: organ donation anonymity
segments.summary: A listener anesthesiologist, Todd, explains that organ donors and recipients usually do not meet for about a year and only after both agree, with identifying details censored, and that some people look for each other online.

segments.title: Sign-off and thanks to Dan Made pottery
segments.summary: Hosts thank Dan of Dan Made pottery for coffee mugs and close the episode.
